meta.title: TechFuelHQ Community GPU Undervolt Results
meta.description: An open, crowdsourced dataset of real GPU undervolt settings and their measured results. Contribute your card via a pull request; git is the moderation queue.
meta.contribute: Submit a pull request adding a row to data/undervolt_results.json. See .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/undervolt-result.md for the required fields and methodology. Every numeric value must cite a resolvable source.

fields.gpu: canonical card model, e.g. 'RTX 5080' or 'RX 9070 XT'
fields.board: AIB/board variant tested, or '' if generic/consensus
fields.tbp_watts: stock total board power in watts
fields.method: MSI Afterburner V/F curve (NVIDIA) or AMD Adrenalin voltage offset/max-voltage (AMD)
fields.setting: human-readable summary of the applied setting
fields.voltage_mv: NVIDIA curve target voltage, or AMD RDNA3 absolute max voltage, in mV (nullable)
fields.offset_mv: AMD negative voltage offset in mV, RDNA4 (nullable)
fields.power_limit_pct: power limit applied; percent of stock for NVIDIA (e.g. 90) or delta for AMD (e.g. -10 or +15); null if untouched
fields.power_saved_w: measured reduction in board power draw, watts (nullable)
fields.temp_drop_c: measured hotspot/junction temperature drop in C (nullable)
fields.fps_delta_pct: measured performance change in percent: + gain, 0 parity, - loss (nullable)
fields.stability_hours: hours held stable under the stated test (nullable)
fields.source_url: primary resolvable source for the numbers
fields.date: YYYY-MM-DD the row was added or last verified
fields.flagged: true if the outlier-flag script flagged this row (do not set by hand)
fields.flag_reason: why it was flagged (set by the script)

results.test_method: Long demanding-game sessions + Superposition loops that hold the card at the locked clock (FurMark does NOT validate a curve undervolt)

results.setting: -100 mV offset (power limit left at stock)
results.test_method: Stress-tested in a demanding game after stepping the offset down from -40 mV; validated in real play, not just a short benchmark
Loop a demanding title / stress test (instability shows as crashes or black screens). FE silicon often stable ~925 mV; AIB cards ~950-975 mV.
Extended in-game / ray-tracing stress test (not just synthetics); some cards need +12-25 mV in heavy RT titles.

results.setting: 900 mV @ 2800 MHz (flatten curve above the point)
results.test_method: Several hours in a memory-heavy title (Cyberpunk 2077 / Monster Hunter). Verify your Afterburner build supports 50-series curve editing.

results.setting: 935 mV @ 2955 MHz (via +450 MHz core offset), +1500 memory
results.test_method: Flatten the V/F curve at the target point; achievable clock at 935 mV varies by card (~2932-2945 MHz measured on the source unit).
results.submitter: TechFuelHQ (community-sourced: Esports Tales hands-on + MSI guide)

results.setting: 1100 mV max voltage (~-50 mV vs ~1150 mV stock), power limit +15%
results.test_method: Lower max voltage in 10-15 mV steps; if it crashes/black-screens, raise 10-15 mV and retest (an invalid UV just resets on reboot). Validate with 15-20 min stress + 20-30 min gameplay.

-100 mV reported daily-stable; community reports crashes past ~-170 mV. This is an EFFICIENCY tune: the -30% power limit trades ~7% FPS for large power/thermal savings. A milder -80 to -100 mV at 0% power limit is the performance-neutral option.
